title: Ansible flow designer document

schema_version.description: Format version of this file: 2 for new flows; a 1 stays readable, and Upgrade Flow Format (or the upgrade_format op) moves it to 2 in one undo step.

id.description: Fixed ID of the flow (ULID). Leave it out when writing by hand: Complete IDs adds it. Never change it.

key.description: Short name of the flow: lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Names the generated playbook.

version.description: Bumped once per commit when the design changes (not for layout moves). Tools bump it; do not edit by hand.

goal.description: What the flow achieves, in a sentence.

owner.description: Team or person that owns the flow.

kind.description: Format 1: awx_job (one playbook), awx_workflow (approval segments) or ansible_playbook (local runs only). Format 2 derives it: AWX when a template is named, a workflow when approvals split the flow.

template.description: Name of the AWX job or workflow template.

credentials.description: Format 2: the AWX credentials of the template, by name (machine, vault …). Set Up AWX Template applies them, and records what was chosen.

execution_environment.description: Format 2: the AWX execution environment of the template, by name.

runtime.description: How the flow runs in AWX: a job template, or a workflow when approvals split it.

imported_from.description: Where an imported flow came from, for reference only: a one-time copy

kind.description: What the flow was imported from: an AWX workflow or job template, or a playbook.

template.description: Name of the imported AWX workflow or job template.

id.description: ID of the imported template in AWX.

path.description: Repository path of the imported playbook (or the job template playbook).

maintenance_window.description: Longest time the flow may take, e.g. 4h or 2h30m (Timing lens)

inputs.description: Inputs a run asks for. A host_list input with targets: true seeds the hosts entering the start node.

flow.description: The flow itself: identity, version, goal and the inputs a run asks for.

nodes.description: Nodes of the top level, in any order. Subflow nodes hold their own inner level under subflow.

edges.description: Wires of the top level: an output port of one node to an input port of another node on the same level. One wire per output port.

annotations.description: Format 2: Notes, Sections and Text on the top level. They explain the flow and never run: editing them changes no version.

layout.description: Canvas positions of every node at every level, by node ID (or by key while written by hand). Optional: missing positions are laid out automatically.

node.description: The node the decision is about (open_on_purpose, drift_ignored; accepted except some lens findings).

port.description: open_on_purpose: the fail port left open on purpose.

kind.description: Format 2: accepted, with finding saying what (port:<port>, drift:<item>, lens:<finding id>, check:<code>[:<subject>]). Format 1: open_on_purpose (a fail port stays unwired on purpose; hosts stop there), drift_ignored (design and code differ on purpose), finding_accepted (a lens finding is expected).

item.description: drift_ignored: the drift item kept as it is

finding.description: accepted: what is accepted (port:, drift:, lens: or check:); finding_accepted: the lens finding kept as expected

reason.description: Why. Required in practice: the designer asks for it.

by.description: Who decided (Git user name). Tools fill it in.

at.description: When (a date), when the writer knows it.

items.description: One decision. kind decides which fields it needs.

decisions.description: Choices people made about the design: a fail port left open on purpose, a drift item or a lens finding kept as it is.

ulid.description: A ULID: 26 characters, digits and uppercase letters (no I, L, O, U). Written by the designer and tools; never invent one by hand.

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits and single dashes, e.g. backup-config.

nodeRef.description: A node: its ID, or its key while the file is written by hand. 'Complete IDs' (designer quick fix, or the flow_complete_ids tool) replaces keys with IDs.

type.description: Value type. host_list is a list of inventory hosts or groups.

required.description: Inputs: a run must provide a value.

default.description: Inputs: value used when none is given.

from.description: Where the value comes from: <node_key>.<output> (an earlier node's output, on this level or around it), flow.<input> (a flow input), <subflow_key>.<input> inside that subflow (its input), or impl.register[.path] (outputs: the bound task's registered result). A subflow's outputs name an inner step's output (<step>.<output>); without from, the inner output of the same name.

targets.description: Flow inputs only: this host_list input seeds the start node's host set.

description.description: Flow inputs: what the input is for, in words. The launch dialog, the run prompts and the AWX survey show it.

contract.description: Named inputs or outputs: name -> field.

port.description: A port name. Which ports a node has depends on its type: see the port catalog. Parallel branch ports are branch_1, branch_2, ...

node.description: The node: its ID, or its key while written by hand.

port.description: Port name: an output (from) or an input (to) of that node.

portref.description: One end of a wire: a node and one of its ports.

id.description: Fixed ID of the wire (ULID). Leave it out when writing by hand: Complete IDs adds it.

from.description: The output port the hosts leave from.

to.description: The input port they enter (usually in).

edge.description: A wire from an output port to an input port on the same level. Its hosts are the hosts that took that output.

ref.description: Fully qualified module or role name (e.g. ansible.builtin.ping, netops.baseline), or the playbook path in the repository.

collection_version.description: Collection version the binding was made against.

params.description: Module parameters or role variables. Jinja may reference inputs by name.

register.description: Variable that keeps the task result; outputs read it with from: impl.register.

keywords.description: Ansible task keywords written on the generated task as they are (module and role bindings). Jinja may reference inputs by name; when, changed_when and failed_when are Jinja tests without braces. What the flow models itself is set there instead: register (impl.register), tags, become, timeout, retries, delay and until (settings), handlers (steps with when: <register> is changed), block and rescue (subflows and failure paths).

when.description: Jinja test without braces (or a list, all must hold): hosts for which it is false skip the task and leave through ok_hosts.

changed_when.description: Jinja test without braces that decides whether the result counts as changed; may read the registered result.

failed_when.description: Jinja test without braces that decides whether the task failed; may read the registered result.

loop.description: List to run the task over, usually Jinja ("{{ interfaces }}"); each item is item (or loop_control.loop_var).

loop_control.description: Loop options: loop_var, index_var, label, pause, extended.

ignore_errors.description: true: a failure is ignored and the host leaves through ok_hosts instead of failed_hosts.

delegate_to.description: Run the task on this host instead (e.g. localhost), on behalf of each arriving host.

delegate_facts.description: With delegate_to: facts go to the delegated host.

run_once.description: Run the task once for the batch, on the first host; the result applies to every host.

no_log.description: Hide the task result in the log (use for secrets).

check_mode.description: true: always run in check mode; false: run for real even in check mode.

diff.description: Show or hide the diff of changes for this task.

environment.description: Environment variables for the task (a map, or Jinja).

become_flags.description: Extra flags for the become method.

connection.description: Connection plugin for this task (local, network_cli, ...).

throttle.description: Most hosts running this task at the same time.

async.description: Run in the background for at most this many seconds.

poll.description: Seconds between status checks of an async task (0: do not wait).

vars.description: Task variables; for a role binding, put role variables in params instead.

module_defaults.description: Default parameters for modules run by this task.

debugger.description: When to start the task debugger (always, never, on_failed, ...).

^with_[a-z_]+$.description: A with_<lookup> loop (with_items, with_dict, ...): prefer loop.

impl.description: What the node runs: an Ansible module, a role or a playbook. null or absent: the node runs as a TODO stub (walking skeleton).

additionalProperties.description: Top-left corner of the node on the canvas, in pixels.

layout.description: Positions by node ID (or by key while written by hand).

annotation.description: A Note, Section or Text on a level (format 2): it explains the flow and never runs.

id.description: Unique among the nodes, wires and annotations of the flow. 'Complete IDs' adds it when written by hand.

key.description: Unique among the annotations of its level, e.g. note-1 or section-2; tools name it by this key.

kind.description: note (default): a sticky note; section: a titled region behind nodes, dragged with what is inside it; text: words with no background.

x.description: Left edge on the canvas, in pixels; for a note on a node, from the node's left edge.

y.description: Top edge on the canvas, in pixels; for a note on a node, from the node's top edge.

width.description: Width in pixels. Absent: the kind's default (note 200, section 480, text fits its words).

height.description: Height in pixels. Absent: the kind's default (note 120, section 320, text fits its words).

color.description: Background of a note, tint of a section, color of text. Absent: yellow (notes), gray (sections, text).

on.description: Notes only: the node on the same level this note is about. The note moves with it, is deleted with it, and its text becomes a comment above the node's code.

size.description: Text only: small, medium (default) or large.

text.description: Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, - bullet lists and [links](https://...). A section's title; the words of a text.

id.description: Fixed ID of the node (ULID). Leave it out when writing by hand: Complete IDs adds it. Never change it.

key.description: Short name, unique on its level: lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Wires and from: references may use it.

type.description: start (one, on the top level; hosts enter), end (hosts leave; outcome success or failed), task, subflow (has an inner level), decision (true/false per host), approval (a person approves), parallel (branches), join (branches meet).

title.description: Human name shown on the canvas.

intent.description: What the node should do, in a sentence. Skeleton runs print it.

status.description: How far the node is built: draft (an idea), specified (has inputs or outputs), implemented (bound to code; a control node once complete), tested (a passing run, or by hand with a reason). In format 2 it follows the node's content (a subflow: its lowest step) and the designer keeps it so; tested needs a `tested` record.

tested.description: Format 2: why the node counts as tested. A passing run (run, flow_version, commit) or a reason given by hand (reason, by, at).

flow_version.description: The flow version that run executed.

commit.description: The commit the run executed (AWX runs).

reason.description: Why it counts as tested, given by hand.

by.description: Who gave the reason (Git user name).

inputs.description: Values the node needs, usually from: an earlier node or a flow input.

outputs.description: Values the node produces for later nodes.

ports.description: Optional ports enabled beyond the type defaults (e.g. unreachable, timeout, always on a task).

impl.description: What the node runs: a module, a role or a playbook. Absent: a TODO stub.

origin.description: Where an import took this step from (Re-import from Source matches by it).

design.description: Fingerprint of the step as imported: a different one means it was changed here.

gone.description: The task is no longer in the source (set by Re-import; the step stays).

ref.description: Format 2: this subflow is a copy of a subflow in another flow (a shared subflow). Edit the source flow, then Update; Unlink makes the copy this flow's own.

from.description: <flow file, relative to this flow's folder>#<subflow key path in it>

version.description: The source flow's version the copy was made from.

design.description: Fingerprint of the copy as it was made: a different one means it was changed here.

undo.description: What reverses the node: the Rollback pattern binds this node's undo step to it.

condition.description: Decision nodes: Jinja test without braces, evaluated per host; it reads the node's inputs

join_mode.description: Join nodes: per host, all = every branch delivered the host (default), any = at least one

branches.description: Parallel nodes: number of branch ports branch_1..branch_n (default 2)

handler.description: Format 1 name of purpose. Marks a failure handler node (what kind of handling it does)

purpose.description: Format 2: what the node is for in failure handling (rollback, notify, retry, exclude); the patterns set it, and a Rollback is found by it.

max_fail_percentage.description: Fail the whole node when more than this share of hosts fail.

serial.description: Batch size or percentage for rolling execution.

rolling.description: Subflows: hosts per batch (a number, or a percentage like 25%) through every step inside, one batch after another. The steps run in one play with this serial; a step that needs plays of its own (a subflow, approval, parallel, join, playbook binding, inventory_target, or its own serial or max_fail_percentage) stops it (rolling-unsupported).

timeout.description: Task timeout, e.g. 300 or 5m. Hosts that time out leave through the timeout port.

retries.description: Retries after the first try (module steps): the task runs once, then up to retries more times before a host fails (retries 12: 13 tries). Without until, a step stops retrying on its first success.

delay.description: Seconds between tries (Ansible delay, default 5). A step polls for at most (retries + 1) x timeout + retries x delay.

until.description: Poll until this holds: a Jinja test without braces, e.g. wait_ha_result.json.results | length == 2. It reads the step's registered result (impl.register, else <key with _ for ->_result) and its inputs. Module steps only; retries sets the attempts.

become.description: Run with privilege escalation. Format 2: set on a subflow, it applies to the steps inside (the nearest setting wins).

become_user.description: Format 2: whom to become (Ansible become_user); set on a subflow, it applies inside. Format 1 writes it as a task keyword.

inventory_target.description: Run the node's work on this host pattern instead of the arriving hosts (they leave together afterwards).

tags.description: Extra Ansible tags for the generated play.

annotations.description: Format 2: Notes, Sections and Text on the inner level.

layout.description: Old place for inner positions: read, never written (positions live in the top-level layout).

in.description: The inner node that receives the hosts entering the subflow.

additionalProperties.description: Inner outputs leaving through this port.

outputs.description: Exits: a parent port name -> the inner outputs that leave through it.

boundary.description: How hosts enter and leave the subflow.

subflow.description: Subflow nodes: the inner level and how hosts enter and leave it.

node.description: A step of the flow. Its type decides its ports; its status says how far it is built.
The inner node: its ID, or its key while written by hand.

reason.description: Why hosts leave the subflow here (shown on the exit wire)

exitref.description: An inner output that leaves the subflow.

description: An Ansible flow: a graph of typed nodes wired port to port. Hosts travel along the wires; every control port carries the hosts that took it. The designer edits this file; tools and AI assistants may write it too.
